text:
table of contents for "Trading in the Zone" by Mark Douglas

what you see: attitude, mindset, responsibility, accountability

what you don't see: fundamentals, technicals, macro

in understanding this, u can recognize almost immediately when someone is wired in a way that ensures they will never succeed in markets

it may be easiest to define the "right" temperament, thru the absence of wrongs.

negative traits for trading markets:
-blame
-envy
-victim mentality
-always "the market's fault"
-being right > making money
-sore loser, unable to take a clean L
-always complaining, bitching, whining
-never talks P&L or cost basis
-lives in avoidance of pain, failure, judgment, criticism
-focuses on other people's flaws, never on their own

no one is ever "better" than them, there's always an excuse

no ownership, no accountability for why they are where they are

if ur wired this way, u will always have company

but there is just no room for any of it in markets

P&L is too bright of a light, it cuts right through all blame and deflection, it leaves u nowhere to hide

if u even want a tiny chance of success, 100% of everything has to go on ur shoulders

and that's just the ante

out of everyone sitting at the "big boys" table, 99.99% will go on to underperform the index

why did Douglas write this book? in his words..."to convince the trader that it's his attitude and 'state of mind' that determine his results."

hard truth right there...

"the ten cardinal rules" -- this is from Ari Kiev's book

man coached everyone from L/S PM's to US Olympic athletes

I share it bc what u see at the highest level, couldnt be more simple and basic.

-"what emotion am I feeling right now"
-"how do I react to stress"
-"out of all the possible styles, what works for my temperament"

this is what waits for u at the top of the mountain

u may as well start grappling with it now

and u may as well stop asking the world -- or asking LLMs -- questions which can only be answered by the man in the mirror...
